00143 /**
00144  * @brief Constants defining drawing effects for lines, rectangles, triangles,
00145  * and spans.  These constants can be combined.
00146  */
00147 typedef enum HxDrawFlags_t
00148 {
00149     /**
00150      * @brief Use none of the effects
00151      */
00152     kHxDrawNoFX            = 0,
00153 
00154     /**
00155      * @brief Use alpha blending
00156      */
00157     kHxDrawBlend           = (1 << 0),
00158 
00159     /**
00160      * @brief Write to the destination only if the destination pixel matches
00161      * the destination color key
00162      */
00163     kHxDrawDstColorKey     = (1 << 1),
00164 
00165     /**
00166      * @brief Multiply the color's rgb channels by the alpha channel before
00167      * drawing
00168      */
00169     kHxDrawSrcPremultiply  = (1 << 2),
00170 
00171     /**
00172      * @brief Modulate the destination color with the destination alpha
00173      */
00174     kHxDrawDstPremultiply  = (1 << 3),
00175 
00176     /**
00177      * @brief Divide the color by the alpha before writing the data to the
00178      * destination
00179      */
00180     kHxDrawDemultiply      = (1 << 4),
00181 
00182     /**
00183      * @brief Bitwise XOR the destination pixels with the specified color after
00184      * premultiplication
00185      */
00186     kHxDrawXOR             = (1 << 5),
00187 
00188     kHxDrawFlagsMask       = kHxDrawBlend | kHxDrawBlend | kHxDrawDstColorKey
00189                               | kHxDrawSrcPremultiply | kHxDrawDstPremultiply
00190                               | kHxDrawDemultiply | kHxDrawXOR
00191 } HxDrawFlags_t;

00194 /**
00195  * @brief Constants for selecting the Porter-Duff composition technique.
00196  * These constants should not be combined.
00197  * Pixel.r = (Source.r * FS) + (Dest.r * FD)
00198  * Pixel.g = (Source.g * FS) + (Dest.g * FD)
00199  * Pixel.b = (Source.b * FS) + (Dest.b * FD)
00200  */
00201 
00202 typedef enum HxBlendPorterDuffRule_t
00203 {
00204     /**
00205      * @brief The default blend function.
00206      * FS = Source Alpha        FD = 1.0 - Source Alpha
00207      */
00208     kHxBlendNone = 0,
00209 
00210     /**
00211      * @brief Neither the source nor destination are drawn.
00212      * FS = 0.0                 FD = 0.0
00213      */
00214     kHxBlendClear,
00215 
00216     /**
00217      * @brief The source is the only surface drawn.
00218      * FS = 1.0                 FD = 0.0
00219      */
00220     kHxBlendSource,
00221 
00222     /**
00223      * @brief The source is drawn above the destination.
00224      * FS = 1.0                 FD = 1.0 - Source Alpha
00225      */
00226     kHxBlendSourceOver,
00227 
00228     /**
00229      * @brief The destination is drawn above the destination.
00230      * FS = 1.0 - Dest Alpha    FD = 1.0
00231      */
00232     kHxBlendDestOver,
00233 
00234     /**
00235      * @brief The source is drawn where the destination overlaps.
00236      * FS = Dest Alpha          FD = 0.0
00237      */
00238     kHxBlendSourceIn,
00239 
00240     /**
00241      * @brief The destination surface is drawn where the source overlaps.
00242      * FS = 0.0                 FD = Source Alpha
00243      */
00244     kHxBlendDestIn,
00245 
00246     /**
00247      * @brief The source surface is drawn except where the destination overlaps.
00248      * FS = 1.0 - Dest Alpha    FD = 0.0
00249      */
00250     kHxBlendSourceOut,
00251 
00252     /**
00253      * @brief The destination surface is drawn except where the source overlaps.
00254      * FS = 0.0                 FD = 1.0 - Source Alpha
00255      */
00256     kHxBlendDestOut,
00257 
00258     /**
00259      * @brief The destination surface is drawn. Where the source overlaps,
00260      * the source will be drawn instead.
00261      * FS = Dest Alpha          FD = 1.0 - Source Alpha
00262      */
00263     kHxBlendSourceATop,
00264 
00265     /**
00266      * @brief The source surface is drawn. Where the destination overlaps,
00267      * the destination will be drawn instead.
00268      * FS = 1.0 - Dest Alpha    FD = Source Alpha
00269      */
00270     kHxBlendDestATop,
00271 
00272     /**
00273      * @brief The source and destination are both drawn and colors are
00274      * added together where they intersect.
00275      * FS = 1.0                 FD = 1.0
00276      */
00277     kHxBlendAdd,
00278 
00279     /**
00280      * @brief The source and destination are drawn where there is no
00281      * intersection.
00282      * FS = 1.0 - Dest Alpha    FD = 1.0 - Source Alpha
00283      */
00284     kHxBlendXOR
00285 
00286 
00287 } HxBlendPorterDuffRule_t;

00604 /**
00605  * @brief               Draw the highlight panel object
00606  *
00607  * Several applications, including System Preferences, are designed with
00608  * common elements.  One of these elements is the panel on the left side of
00609  * the application window, drawn with a common background bitmap and one or
00610  * more lists.  In System Preferences, for example, there is one list of
00611  * preference sets.  Each of the lists are highlighted with an alpha-blended
00612  * shape.
00613  *
00614  * HxGraphicsDrawPanelHighlight provides a way to draw this alpha-blended
00615  * shape.
00616  *
00617  * Normally, pWidget points to the panel container.  pRect points to the bounds
00618  * of the shape.  The rectangle must not be smaller than the minimum dimensions
00619  * required by this shape.  In the current implementation, HX_INVALID_ARG is
00620  * returned if pRect has a width < 10 or height < 20.  In general, the pRect
00621  * should not be smaller than the bounds of the list containing two strings.
00622  *
00623  * @param pWidget       IN:     Pointer to widget
00624  * @param pRect         IN:     Pointer to rectangle
00625  *
00626  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.
00627  *                              Returns HX_INVAREA if the widget's clipping
00628  *                              region is empty.

00901  * source and destination images may be the same.  The main application window

00903  * window is used for the destination image if pDstImage is NULL.
00904  *
00905  * If the pSrcRect argument is NULL, the entire source image is used, and
00906  * clipped to the destination if appropriate.  If pSrcRect argument is not
00907  * NULL, the specified bounds of the source image is drawn.

00910  * @param pDstImage     IN:     Pointer to destination image, or NULL

00914  *
00915  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.
00916  *                              Returns HX_INVAREA if the widget's clipping
00917  *                              region is empty, or if the bounds of pSrcRect
00918  *                              does not include any portion of pSrcImage.
00919  *
00920  **/
00921 HxResult HxGraphicsBlit(HxImage_t* pSrcImage, HxImage_t* pDstImage,
00922                         const HxRectangle_t* pSrcRect, int32_t x, int32_t y);

01010 /**
01011  * @brief               Force a screen update
01012  *
01013  * HxGraphicsForceUpdate causes an immediate screen update.
01014  *
01015  * Normally, screen updates occur when the system is idle, after the
01016  * application enters the event loop by calling HxWindowEventLoop.  
01017  * HxGraphicsForceUpdate can be used to force the blitter to flush its graphics
01018  * pipeline, independent from the screen update, when the application draws
01019  * directly into the frame buffer using the HxGraphics API.
01020  *
01021  * Use HxWidgetDraw to force the screen update when drawing widgets rather
01022  * than the HxGraphics graphic primitives.
01023  *
01024  * pWidget can be an onscreen window or an offscreen canvas. 
01025  *
01026  * @param pWidget       IN:     Pointer to widget
01027  * @param pClip         IN:     Pointer to region to update
01028  *
01029  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.
01030  *
01031  **/
01032 HxResult HxGraphicsForceUpdate(HxWidget_t* pWidget, HxRegion_t* pClip);
